Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations, globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and is sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and gain valuable skills assisting our communications team in our public relations and social media efforts. About Keeper Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com . About the Role The Communications Intern will be mentored by and report to Keeper’s Communications Director and will be responsible for supporting the Communications and Social Media teams on daily tasks and projects. Aprio is seeking an Aprio is seeking an Accounting and Implementation Manager  to lead restaurant, franchise, and hospitality platform implementations, re-implementations, and optimization initiatives that connect accounting, operations, and technology. In this role, you will partner with clients and our accounting team to translate complex accounting and operational needs into practical configurations, integrations, workflows, controls, reporting structures, and training across platforms including Restaurant365 (R365), QuickBooks Online (QBO), Sage Intacct, and other industry-specific tools. You will serve as a trusted technology resource across the practice â driving implementation quality, enabling team capability, and building a repeatable, scalable delivery model. This is a high-impact opportunity for a systems-minded professional who brings both accounting fluency and a practical approach to helping people get the most from their technology.

\n


What You'll Gain/ Impact
  • Clients will have platform environments that support reliable accounting, disciplined operations, strong controls, and sustainable growth
  • Our accounting team will have the tools, training, documentation, and responsive support needed to serve clients efficiently across multiple platforms
  • Implementations will move forward with clear ownership, clean master data, disciplined testing, timely decisions, and fewer surprises
  • Your improvements will reduce manual work, strengthen operating data, and build a repeatable, high-value delivery capability across the practice
 


Key Responsibilities

Platform Implementation & Re-Implementation

  • Lead implementations and re-implementations across restaurant, franchise, and hospitality platforms â including R365, QBO, Sage Intacct, and other industry-specific tools â from discovery and design through configuration, testing, cutover, and stabilization

  • Guide data readiness, testing, decisions, and go-live activities while helping the accounting team resolve issues that affect service delivery, close, and reporting

Client Accounting & Financial Reporting

  • Own accounting and financial reporting for assigned clients, including agreed-upon deliverables, deadlines, responsibilities, and scope.

Restaurant Operations Configuration

  • Build and govern inventory items, categories, locations, count practices, costing methods, and location availability

  • Configure labor scheduling, job codes, forecasting inputs, and targets; establish best-practice routines for counts, waste, transfers, receiving, recipe maintenance, and exception review

Platform Optimization & Process Design

Integrations, Data & Reporting

Required:

  • Background in outsourced accounting, CAS, public accounting, or another multi-client professional-services environment
  • Experience improving accounting, reporting, analytics, or client-service workflows through technology or automation 
  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Business, Hospitality Management, Project Management, or a related field
  • Five or more years of ERP implementation, accounting technology, restaurant systems or operations, systems consulting, or related professional-services experience
  • Hands-on experience with Restaurant365 (R365), QuickBooks Online (QBO), Sage Intacct, or comparable restaurant, franchise, or hospitality platform implementation, administration, optimization, or support
  • Working knowledge of close, reporting, banking, daily sales, AP, inventory, purchasing, item mapping, units of measure, recipes, POS/PMIX, payroll, labor scheduling, and controls
  • Strong client-facing project leadership, facilitation, documentation, problem-solving, change-management, and communication skills

Preferred:

  • R365 certification, Sage Intacct certification, or advanced experience across accounting and operations modules
  • Restaurant, franchise, hospitality, multi-entity, or multi-location experience, including POS/PMIX, inventory, recipe costing, labor, AP, payroll, banking, and reporting tools
  • Experience across multiple restaurant, franchise, or hospitality platforms such as QBO, Sage Intacct, or other industry-specific ERP and accounting solutions

\n

Whether you are just starting out, looking to advance into management or searching for your next leadership role, Aprio offers an opportunity to grow with a future-focused, innovative firm.

Familiarity with Oracle ERP Cloud and SFDC release feature review and technical impact assessment. Familiarity with pipeline configuration: triggering regression runs on pull requests and release candidate builds. Working knowledge of version control (Git / GitHub or GitLab): branching, pull requests, and code review workflows. Basic scripting capability in Python, Shell, or PowerShell for test utility automation and pipeline support. Understanding of containerized test environments (Docker); experience running tests in ephemeral containers is a plus. Jira for defect tracking, test coverage reporting, and sprint participation. Experience writing and maintaining test documentation: test plans, test cases, regression logs, and release readiness summaries. Ability to work cross-functionally with ERP Functional Analysts, ERP Technical Developers, and DevOps engineers. Familiarity with SOX compliance, ITGC controls, and ERP change management practices. Preferred Qualifications Oracle Fusion certification or formal training in Oracle ERP Cloud modules. Experience with SaaS QA automation in a high-growth technology company environment. Exposure to OIC (Oracle Integration Cloud) or MuleSoft integration testing. Familiarity with Salesforce test automation frameworks beyond Tosca (Selenium, Provar, or equivalent). Prior experience working with AMS or managed services vendors in an ERP context. Knowledge of Oracle quarterly release cycles and technical impact assessments. title: Channel Account Manager
description: Headquarters: USA - Remote About Ping Identity: At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. They come to cultivate it. Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear. While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work. We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management. We are seeking a strategic, field-facing Channel Account Manager to lead channels for Ping’s Enterprise team. Ping’s Enterprise sales team is the new-logo engine for companies with less than $2B in revenue and spans the commercial segment of the USA. This team has a track record of exceeding targets, and your role will help them to work with partners to drive a repeatable, scalable sales motion. You will spend meaningful time in the field with partner and Ping sales teams, building rep-to-rep engagement and turning joint account plans into qualified pipeline and closed business. You will also help organize regional partner engagements that bring the right teams together around target accounts and repeatable go-to-market plays. This is a builder role for someone who is thoughtful, positive, curious, and ready to turn strategy into action. You Will: Own the Enterprise partner strategy and plan, with a clear focus on new-logo acquisition, regional coverage, partner priorities, and measurable outcomes. Build trusted relationships with partner executives, alliance leaders, sellers, technical teams, and delivery organizations, while working in the field with partners and Ping sales teams to identify target accounts and create joint account plans. Drive rep-to-rep engagement between Ping sellers and partner sellers, helping teams identify opportunities, coordinate pursuits, and progress new-logo deals. Set up and support regional partner events, including field meetings, account-mapping sessions, enablements, workshops, roundtables, and other activities designed to create partner-to-partner engagement and qualified pipeline. Develop repeatable partner go-to-market plays and practical enablement that help partners position Ping Identity, engage new enterprise accounts, and progress opportunities. Partner with Enterprise sales, Partner Solutions Engineering, marketing, services, and product teams to remove friction and help partners win and deliver successfully. Track partner activity, event engagement, sourced and influenced pipeline, new-logo progress, and follow-through; use the data to focus time and investment where it will have the greatest impact. Deliver measurable impact by expanding productive partner coverage, increasing partner-led new-logo pipeline, improving rep-to-rep engagement, and turning regional activity into repeatable growth. You Have: 10+ years of experience in channel, alliances, partner sales, or a related go-to-market role in enterprise technology. Experience working with partners to acquire new customers and build sourced or influenced pipeline in the Enterprise market. Experience managing or developing relationships with integrators, resellers, delivery partners, and/or distributors. A track record of building partner programs, joint account plans, field motions, or other repeatable go-to-market plays—not simply managing existing relationships. Strong field presence and the ability to engage credibly with partner executives, sellers, technical teams, and Ping sales leaders. Excellent communication and facilitation skills, including the ability to create productive rep-to-rep conversations and turn meetings into clear next steps. A positive, practical, and collaborative approach; you create momentum, follow through on commitments, and are comfortable operating in a changing environment. Willingness to travel regularly and spend meaningful time with partners, customers, and internal teams in the field. Bonus Points If You Have: Experience in cybersecurity, identity and access management, or another complex enterprise technology category. Experience working with both national and regional partners, or building partner coverage in new territories. Experience planning and executing regional partner events, roundtables, workshops, or field marketing programs. Experience creating partner enablement programs, certifications, technical workshops, or sales plays. Experience working with sales development, account executives, and partner sellers to create net-new opportunities. Enthusiasm for representing the company at partner forums, industry events, roundtables, and other public-facing engagements. A relevant degree or equivalent experience, and/or cybersecurity or channel-related certifications. Salary Range: $88,000–$132,000 base + Commission In accordance with Colorado’s Equal Pay for Equal Work Act (SB 19-085) the approximate compensation range for this role in Colorado is listed above. Final compensation for this role will be determined by various factors, such as knowledge, skills, and abilities. Life at Ping: We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day. Here are just a few of the things that make Ping special: A company culture that empowers you to do your best work. Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone. Regular company and team bonding events. Competitive benefits and perks. Global volunteering and community initiatives Our Benefits: Generous PTO & Holiday Schedule Parental Leave Progressive Healthcare Options Retirement Programs Opportunity for Education Reimbursement Commuter Offset (Specific locations) Ping is the collective sum of all our individual experiences, backgrounds and influences and we pride ourselves in growing and learning together. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment where everyone’s individuality is respected and everyone has an Identity. In recruiting for new colleagues, we welcome the unique contributions you can bring and encourage you to be your best self. We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. description: Headquarters: Remote About Carrot: Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide. Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com . The Opportunity Carrot is looking for a Director, Information Security to lead the security program that protects the highly sensitive fertility and family-building data of members around the world. You will set the security strategy, own both corporate security (GRC, incident response, security awareness, vendor risk) and product security (application, cloud and infrastructure security, secure development lifecycle), and serve as the trusted voice on Carrot's security posture with executives, auditors, and enterprise customers. Day to day, you will balance setting direction with staying close to the work: prioritizing risk with Engineering and IT, guiding audit and certification cycles, coaching a small and talented team, and joining customer conversations where security is part of the buying decision. Carrot has already earned SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS compliance, so this role is about taking a strong foundation to the next level of maturity, not starting from scratch. What makes this role different is the combination of stakes and influence. Few security leaders get to protect data this personal, at global scale, while working directly with executive leadership and shaping how a health platform is built, sold, and trusted. What You’ll Own In this role, you will: Lead Carrot's security strategy and roadmap, using a recognized maturity model (such as C2M2 or NIST CSF) to prioritize investments and report progress to executive leadership Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and raw.title: Carrot: Director, Information Security
raw.description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com.

The Opportunity 

Carrot is looking for a Director, Information Security to lead the security program that protects the highly sensitive fertility and family-building data of members around the world. You will set the security strategy, own both corporate security (GRC, incident response, security awareness, vendor risk) and product security (application, cloud and infrastructure security, secure development lifecycle), and serve as the trusted voice on Carrot's security posture with executives, auditors, and enterprise customers.

Day to day, you will balance setting direction with staying close to the work: prioritizing risk with Engineering and IT, guiding audit and certification cycles, coaching a small and talented team, and joining customer conversations where security is part of the buying decision. Carrot has already earned SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS compliance, so this role is about taking a strong foundation to the next level of maturity, not starting from scratch.

What makes this role different is the combination of stakes and influence. Few security leaders get to protect data this personal, at global scale, while working directly with executive leadership and shaping how a health platform is built, sold, and trusted.

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

  • Lead Carrot's security strategy and roadmap, using a recognized maturity model (such as C2M2 or NIST CSF) to prioritize investments and report progress to executive leadership
  • Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure SDLC)
  • Partner with Engineering, especially the Internal Platform team, to build security into how Carrot designs, ships, and operates its systems, going beyond compliance
  • Lead internal risk assessments across application, cloud, and corporate environments and turn the results into prioritized technical safeguards
  • Own the compliance portfolio, including SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, and prepare Carrot for additional frameworks such as ISO 27001 as the business requires
  • Direct incident response readiness, including playbooks, tabletop exercises, executive communication, and post-incident learning
  • Represent Carrot's security posture to employers, health plans, and health systems through security reviews, questionnaires, and strategic sales conversations
  • Work with Legal and Privacy to meet global data protection requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) for member health data
  • Build, coach, and grow the security team, balancing hands-on execution with delegation as the team scales
  • Manage the security budget, tooling, and vendor relationships, and tailor security guidance for a remote-first workforce and physical offices

What Success Looks Like  

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

  • A documented, executive-endorsed security strategy and multi-year roadmap with clear priorities, owners, and measures of progress
  • Clean outcomes on recurring audits and certifications (SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS), with remediation items closed on schedule
  • A tested incident response program, with regular tabletop exercises completed and lessons learned built back into the program
  • A measurable reduction in high-risk vulnerabilities and open security findings, with remediation timelines agreed on with Engineering
  • A living risk register and vendor security review process that leaders rely on to make decisions
  • A security team with defined roles, clear growth paths, and the right capacity for Carrot's growth, including key hires made
  • Faster, more consistent security reviews for Sales and Customer Success, with fewer escalations from enterprise customers
  • A clear plan, and visible progress, on any additional frameworks the business prioritizes, such as ISO 27001

About You

You likely have:

  • A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 10+ years of experience in technology, including 5+ years in information security and at least 3 years leading security teams
  • A security certification such as CISSP or CISM
  • Experience leading the security function at a late-stage startup, scale-up, or public company
  • Working depth in healthcare data protection and privacy frameworks, including HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA/CPRA
  • Experience overseeing enterprise frameworks and audits such as SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001
  • Strong knowledge of application, network, and cloud security (AWS and Azure) and frameworks such as NIST CSF and OWASP
  • Experience running core security programs, including incident response, risk management, vulnerability management, penetration testing, and security awareness
  • Executive-level communication skills and confidence engaging customers and sales teams on security requirements
  • Experience managing budget and allocating resources across people, tools, and vendors

 

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

  • Experience leading security through a major company event such as an IPO, acquisition, or large-scale audit cycle
  • A background in healthcare, digital health, or another highly regulated, high-trust environment
  • Experience leading security in a remote-first, globally distributed company
  • Familiarity with compliance automation platforms such as Drata
  • Experience building a security engineering practice alongside platform and infrastructure teams

 

Why This Role Matters

Members trust Carrot with some of the most personal information a person can share, often during some of the most meaningful moments of their lives. Protecting that trust is not a back-office function. It is what allows employers, health plans, and health systems to bring Carrot to millions of people worldwide.

As Carrot grows, security leadership shapes how we build, how we sell, and how we show up for customers. In this role, you will make security a strength that members and customers can see and rely on, and build a team that keeps raising the bar as the business scales.

Why Candidates Join Carrot

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

  • A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
  • A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.
  • Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.
  • The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

 

Compensation: 

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their lives inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $188,000.00 - $245,000.00. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. 

 

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com

 

A Note on AI

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot?

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com. 

 

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/carrot-director-information-security

About Flexport: 

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year. 

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

What you'll do

There is no MSSP and no tier-1 queue here. Detection & Response engineers own their detections end to end: you write them, you tune them, and your team is paged when they fire. The security team is spread across the globe with a follow-the-sun pager rotation so nobody is paged at 3am local.

The adversaries are real. The business is growing fast and the threat surface is growing with it. Defining the necessary telemetry is part of the job.

Detection engineering

  • Build and tune detections across endpoint, identity, SaaS, and cloud, treating them as software: version-controlled, peer-reviewed, and shipped through the same CI/CD practices the rest of engineering uses.
  • Track detection quality as measured quantities: coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, precision, time-to-detect. We don’t build-and-forget here.

Response & automation

  • Own incident response: triage, contain, remediate, and write the retrospective that turns the incident into a systemic fix.
  • Build automation that removes toil from investigations, and partner closely with the US-based team so context carries across time zones instead of getting lost at handoff.

Telemetry & partnership

  • Define telemetry requirements for new systems before they ship, working with infrastructure and product teams to close visibility gaps rather than discovering them during an incident.
  • Threat hunt proactively across the estate, converting hypotheses into either new detections or documented coverage.

You Should Have

  • Typically 5–8 years of experience in detection engineering, incident response, or threat hunting, with real hands-on time writing and tuning detections. We care more about what you've built than the exact number.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python, Go, or similar) and comfort writing production-grade detection and automation code.
  • Experience with a modern SIEM or detection pipeline (Panther, Elastic, Splunk, or similar). What matters is that you've shipped and tuned detection logic in production.
  • Practical incident response experience: you've led or played a major role in triaging and closing out real security incidents.

Nice to have

  • Experience treating detections as code with CI/CD, peer review, and staged rollout.
  • Experience defining telemetry contracts for systems before they ship, rather than retrofitting logging after an incident.
  • A track record of critically evaluating and verifying AI-assisted work - testing, source-checking, validation - rather than trusting agent output by default. If you haven’t already spotted the em dashes in this job description and already thought about where the hiring manager (hi!) has put hands on keyboard and compared that to where they let the LLM watermarks through, you might not be the right person for the job.
  • Familiarity with cloud-native and Kubernetes telemetry.
  • Experience with fraud or financial-crime detection patterns.

How we work

  • We stay closely aligned with teammates on other continents via Slack, video, and async docs.
  • We have the latest hardware and software, including frontier AI models on day one.
  • We're agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why this role is special

  • You own your detections end to end, no MSSP, no tier-1 queue, no handing your work to someone else to triage.
  • The consequences here are physical, not abstract: a containment decision can stop a customs filing or freight actually moving, which makes the stakes concrete in a way a SaaS control plane rarely is.
  • You'll inherit a real, established estate with legacy telemetry gaps to close, genuinely underexplored surface area, not a well-mined problem.

raw.title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks
raw.description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

 

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

 

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

 

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

 

Requirements

 

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering
  • Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
  • Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
  • Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now
  • A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

 

Nice to have

 

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
  • Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

 

Terms

 

  • US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
  • Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

 

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

title: Graduate Transport Planner
description:
At Curtins, we're an employee-owned engineering consultancy driven by a simple ambition: to create a better built environment for everyone.

For over 65 years, we've delivered practical, innovative and sustainable solutions that make a positive impact on communities across the UK and Ireland. From major regeneration schemes and commercial developments to education, healthcare and residential projects, our work helps shape the places where people live, learn, work and thrive.

As a Graduate Transport Planner, you'll work alongside experienced planners, engineers and consultants, contributing to a wide range of projects while developing the technical and professional skills you need to build your career.

Whether you're interested in transport assessments, active travel & sustainable mobility, highways or public transport, we'll give you the experience, guidance and support to find the areas that interest you most and develop your expertise in development planning.

What you'll be doing

You will support the planning and development process, helping clients bring projects forward from initial concept through to planning approval.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Assisting with the preparation of Transport Assessments and Transport Statements.

  • Supporting the production of Travel Plans and technical planning reports.

  • Analysing traffic, transport and movement data.

  • Assisting with junction assessments and development impact studies.

  • Supporting planning applications for residential, commercial and mixed-use developments.

  • Working alongside planners, civil engineers and other specialists to deliver integrated solutions.

  • Attending client meetings, project discussions and stakeholder consultations.

  • Taking part in wider Curtins activities including STEM outreach, charity initiatives and community projects.

What kind of projects will I get to work on?

You'll be involved in projects across a wide range of sectors, including:

  • Residential developments.

  • Urban regeneration schemes.

  • Commercial and industrial projects.

  • Education and healthcare developments.

  • Mixed-use masterplans.

  • Strategic land and development opportunities.

You'll help assess how developments interact with the transport network and support clients through the planning process, helping turn ideas into deliverable projects.

How will Curtins support my development?

Our goal is simple: to help you become the best engineer you can be.

Through the Curtins Graduate Academy, you'll follow a structured development programme designed to accelerate both your technical and professional growth.

You'll benefit from:

  • A structured graduate development programme.

  • Dedicated mentoring and coaching.

  • Regular technical and professional skills training.

  • Support towards professional registration and Chartership.

  • Exposure to a wide range of projects, clients and sectors.

  • Opportunities to build your network across the business.

You'll be supported by experienced professionals who are genuinely invested in your success and development.

What we're looking for

We're looking for graduates who are curious, analytical and interested in how development projects are planned and delivered.

You'll ideally be studying towards or have recently completed a degree in:

  • Transport Planning

  • Geography

  • Urban Planning

  • Civil Engineering

  • Town Planning

  • Geography or a related discipline

It would also be advantageous to hold an MSc in Transport Planning, Transport Engineering, Urban Planning, or Development Planning.

Most importantly, we're looking for people who share our values:

Integrity - Doing the right thing.

Being Human - Supporting and respecting others.

Curiosity - Asking questions and seeking better solutions.

Impact - Making a meaningful difference through our work.

Why join Curtins?

As an employee-owned business, every person at Curtins contributes to and benefits from our success.

Alongside exciting projects and a supportive culture, you'll enjoy:

  • Industry-leading benefits package.

  • Award-winning training and development programmes.

  • Employee ownership benefits.

  • Opportunities to get involved in STEM, charity and community initiatives.

  • Access to our unique Employee Extras, including our 5-star holiday lodges.

Most importantly, you'll be joining a business where your ideas matter, your development is supported and your contribution makes a real difference.

Build your future with Curtins.

Should you wish to discuss any adjustments to the application process or provide us with feedback please contact hr@curtins.com we would be happy to discuss ways we can make the process more suitable to your needs.

We value diversity and respect all differences in people. We invite enthusiastic individuals who share in our values of teamwork, client focus, integrity, and quality to apply to join us.

We delight in using technology to make security accessible for our customers. Headquarters: Remote

You're the detection engineer people turn to when they ask "what does Microsoft actually see here?" Not the marketing-slide answer, the real map. Which product emits which telemetry, any anticipated ingestion lags, what table or API it lands in, which license tier gates it, how long it survives before it ages out, and where the documentation quietly disagrees with reality. When a new technique drops, your first instinct is to ask which Microsoft signal would catch it, and whether customers have it switched on.

You also know Microsoft never sits still. Hunting tables appear, columns get renamed, Graph versions retire, capability shuffles between SKUs, previews go GA, features quietly vanish, and native alert logic shifts underneath you. You've got a repeatable way of staying ahead of that churn instead of finding out when a detection stops firing. You're comfortable behind a command line and in front of a customer, including scenarios where the conversation isn’t pleasant. If that's you, we'd love to talk! We have an amazing team and believe you'll love getting to know us.

At Expel, we help businesses bridge the cybersecurity talent gap by providing transparent Managed Detection and Response. To do this we build technology to make sure our security analysts are solving important problems, and automation is helping them make better decisions at every step. We delight in using technology to make security accessible for our customers.

What Expel can do for you

  • Make you one of our recognized authorities on Microsoft detection and response — for our SOC, our engineers, our go-to-market teams, and our customers
  • Give you real ownership of Expel's detection coverage across the whole Microsoft security estate
  • Put Microsoft telemetry from across our customer base in front of you — a breadth of real-world environments no single enterprise gets to see
  • Let you write and tune detections in our own rule engine and watch them run against live signal
  • Treat AI tooling (Claude Code and friends) as a first-class part of how you work, not a side experiment
  • Enable you to learn from analysts, data scientists, engineers, and responders responsible for various components of Expel's product and services
  • Provide access to popular EDR, network, SIEM, identity, and cloud technologies well beyond the Microsoft stack
  • Challenge you to push the boundaries of our security vision

What you can do for Expel

  • Own our detection coverage across Defender XDR, Entra ID, Sentinel, Microsoft Graph, Azure, and Microsoft 365 — from raw signal through to shipped, tuned detections
  • Build and maintain a living map of Microsoft security signal: what exists, known ingestion lag, where it lands, what gates it, how long it's kept, and how far you can trust it
  • Track how that signal changes and turn every material change into a concrete action — catching drift before it costs us efficacy
  • Tell us where Microsoft's native detections are strong enough to lean on, where they're noisy or shallow, and where Expel needs its own layer
  • Make SOC analysts faster by automating Microsoft-specific investigative workflows against the Graph, Defender, Sentinel, and Entra APIs
  • Partner with Engineering on our Microsoft integrations — ingestion, API limits and throttling, and schema mapping
  • Answer the hard questions from the SOC, CS, and Sales — and mentor the people asking them
  • Help customers understand what they're actually covered for, what they're missing, and what turning it on would buy them

What you should bring with you

  • Deep, current, hands-on knowledge of the Microsoft security stack — Defender XDR (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365, Cloud Apps), Entra ID, Sentinel, Microsoft Graph, and the Azure and Microsoft 365 control and data planes
  • Fluency in KQL: you can write, read, optimize, and debug non-trivial hunting queries across both Defender Advanced Hunting and Sentinel, and you know how and why the two schemas differ
  • Working knowledge of the Graph and Graph Security APIs, the Defender and Sentinel APIs, and their authentication, permission, versioning, and throttling models
  • A strong grasp of the Entra ID (and legacy Active Directory) identity attack surface — authentication flows, conditional access, OAuth application consent, token theft and replay, hybrid identity and sync, privileged role abuse — and the telemetry each produces
  • Solid understanding of Windows internals and command line tooling, with enough macOS and Linux to keep up with Defender's cross-platform coverage
  • Experience writing, deploying, and tuning custom detections against Microsoft data sets, plus enough non-Microsoft exposure (AWS, GCP, other EDR and SIEM) to keep perspective
  • Proficiency with Python and Sigma, and real fluency using Anthropic tools such as Claude Code to work across systems and data (locally, via MCP, and so on)
  • 5+ years in information technology or security operations, with substantial time spent defending or operating Microsoft environments
  • Excellent tact and diplomacy skills — you can explain Microsoft's limits to an audience that doesn't want to hear about them
  • SC-200, AZ-500, or SC-300 are a plus; demonstrated depth matters considerably more

Work Location

Our headquarters is in Herndon, Virginia. However, we realize that while there is a benefit to in-person interaction, good people don’t all live in Northern Virginia. Remote work is an option for this role.

We are hiring a Head of Technology for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.

Original job posting link

About garden3d

We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.

Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.

Weâre the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer - Development

At Sanctuary Computer weâre building a different type of technology shop â one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX - Design

When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and weâve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

Weâre building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.

Index - Community

Index is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.

We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.

garden3d TK â Media

At garden3d, weâre in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.

We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.

Plus, our partner organizations

Lightphone
Mill
IngredientAI

â°ï¸ The Head of Technology Role

The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.

They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.

Responsibilities & Mandates

ï¸ Systems that hold up

We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.

All in on agentic development

The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering

We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.

Code quality at Sanctuary Computer

Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.

Hiring and empowering the very best

They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

Estimation, scoping and delivery

They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.

The technical voice in new business

Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.

Hardware sense

We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.

The garden3d technology story

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off

Â Special Projects

In addition to day to day responsibilities, hereâs an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years â

  • Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts
  • Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from
  • Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do
  • Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio
  • Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products
  • Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed

Qualifications

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:

Must have:

  • 12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company
  • Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products
  • A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native
  • A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure
  • All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase
  • Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir & Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it
  • Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients
  • A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them
  • Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)

Nice-to-have:

  • A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products
  • Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)
  • Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role
  • Open source projects they've started or maintained
  • Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams
  • Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company
  • A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring
  • Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality

Who you are

The person weâre looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. Theyâre flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work âsmartâ by carefully managing their workflow and team.

How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, weâll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where weâre going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

Compensation

This is a permanent leadership role. If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.

We start with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between $110 - $175 p/hr pending seniority & experience. In the first few weeks of the trial, this individual will propose their own goals to define success in their trial, and present them to our leadership team for approval.

At garden3d, we believe that those who shoulder the most responsibility and create the greatest impact should be paid accordingly. This role greatly favors autonomous, competent & ambitious operators.

â How we work:

We believe that thereâs a better balance between the poles of freelancing & full time, and for that reason we work differently to most shops:

  • Transparency & Ownership:Â We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. Weâre proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community.
  • 150% Carbon Negative: Our studio offsets 150% of the carbon we use to do business each year, dated back to our founding in 2015. We turn down work that is not in-line with our morals, and we encourage our peers to do the same. We have been certified climate neutral since 2021.
  • Strong Morals: Since our founding, we've turned down somewhere between $1mm - $2mm of work that didn't meet our moral standards. (Most of that was DTC brands that can't show a valid sustainability initiative).
  • Async & Decentralized: We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time.
  • Remote Friendly:Â Our company is fluent in remote work, making our workplace more decentralized, and democratized in the process.
  • Ideas & Products:Â In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify & bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio?

â Read more on our Substack, over here.

How to apply

Weâre excited to hear from you! â¤

Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity. Applications with missing or insufficient information will not move forward in the review process.

Our team carefully reviews every complete submission, and we truly appreciate the time and effort you put into applying! :)

title: Cloud Network Engineer
description: Headquarters: Remote United States BeyondTrust is a place where you can bring your purpose to life through the work that you do, creating a safer world through our cybersecurity SaaS portfolio. Our culture of flexibility, trust, and continual learning means you will be recognized for your growth, and for the impact you make on our success. You will be surrounded by people who challenge, support, and inspire you to be the best version of yourself. The Role The Cloud Network Engineer extends BeyondTrust's on-premises networking fundamentals into AWS cloud networking, with a primary focus on architecting and operating FedRAMP-aligned environments. The successful candidate demonstrates strong technical judgment, operational discipline, and the ability to apply practical solutions to complex hybrid network engineering challenges, while serving as the primary liaison between the Network and Cloud Ops teams. What You’ll Do Operate and maintain BeyondTrust's on-premises and cloud network infrastructure, including routing/switching changes, datacenter resource changes, and routine firewall/security group changes end-to-end across on-prem and cloud environments; escalate complex or security-sensitive changes to the Sr. Engineer/SecOps. Design and implement AWS network architectures, including VPCs, Transit Gateway, VPN, Direct Connect, Route 53, and network security controls, aligned with FedRAMP, ISO 27001, and SOX requirements. Lead the CIDR range overlap remediation project by auditing existing on-prem and AWS CIDR allocations, designing a conflict-free addressing plan, and executing remediation/re-IP work with minimal disruption to production traffic. Serve as the primary day-to-day liaison between the Network team and Cloud Ops on network design, shared infrastructure changes, and incident coordination. Mentor Network Administrators and Engineers on cloud networking fundamentals and hybrid connectivity best practices, extending networking expertise into AWS environments. Develop and maintain Infrastructure-as-Code and automation using Terraform, Ansible, Python, contributing reusable modules to the team's shared automation library. Participate in the shared 24x7 on-call rotation, independently resolving Tier-1 and Tier-2 escalations, including cloud connectivity issues. Maintain network diagrams, CIDR/IPAM records, architecture documentation, and SOPs, and provide regular progress updates. Manage vendor relationships for cloud connectivity services, circuit vendors, and network infrastructure procurement and renewals. Work a hybrid or remote schedule depending on geographic proximity to a BeyondTrust office; travel to offices or datacenters as needed (5–10%). What You’ll Bring 3–5 years of total network administration/engineering experience, including 2+ years hands-on AWS cloud networking work with VPC design, Transit Gateway, VPN/Direct Connect, Route 53, network security controls across hybrid environments. Demonstrated proficiency in Administrator/Engineer-level on-premises networking fundamentals. 3-5 hands-on experience with Cisco NX-OS/IOS/IOS-XE, Dell, and Palo Alto equipment. CCNA certification or equivalent hands-on experience Experience implementing and maintaining security controls aligned with industry frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC2, and FedRAMP. Strong documentation and organizational skills — demonstrated ability to produce clear network diagrams, IPAM records, and runbooks that hold up under audit. Strong analytical and cross-team communication skills; comfortable operating as a liaison between technical teams with different priorities. Nice To Have CCNP in progress, or equivalent Network Engineer-level experience. Experience with IPAM tooling such asNetBox, phpIPAM, Infoblox, BlueCat. Experience with Azure networking services and hybrid connectivity. Direct experience supporting a FedRAMP ATO or continuous monitoring (ConMon) process. Formal project management or technical project leadership experience. Proficiency in dynamic routing protocols (EIGRP, BGP) and in identity and access management services including RADIUS, TACACS+, Duo, Okta, and Cisco ISE. Better Together Diversity. Inclusion. They’re more than just words for us. They are the guiding values of how we build our teams, cultivate leaders, and create a culture where people feel connected. We take care of our employees so they can take care of our customers. Customers who come from all walks of life just like us. We hire incredible people from diverse backgrounds because when we are different together, we are stronger together. About Us BeyondTrust is the global identity security leader protecting Paths to Privilege™. Our identity-centric approach goes beyond securing privileges and access, empowering organizations with the most effective solution to manage the entire identity attack surface and neutralize threats, whether from external attacks or insiders. BeyondTrust is leading the charge in transforming identity security to prevent breaches and limit the blast radius of attacks, while creating a superior customer experience and operational efficiencies. We are trusted by 20,000 customers, including 75 of the Fortune 100, and our global ecosystem of partners. Learn more at www.beyondtrust.com . #LI-BS1 To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/beyondtrust-cloud-network-engineer

title: Deployment Strategist
description: Headquarters: Remote - India About the Team The FDE (Forward Deployed Engineering) team is a new, strategic initiative sponsored from the CEO and Founders down. Our mission is to win C-suite-sponsored, high-value AI opportunities by selling and delivering outcomes , not just a platform. You will be part of the founding team, embedded with our most strategic customers from the very first sales call, all the way through to a production-ready solution. You will be the "product manager" for the customer's problem, responsible for the "why" and "what," while our FDEs (Engineers) will be your partners responsible for the "how." Role Description As a Deployment Strategist (DS), you are the critical bridge between a customer's multi-million-dollar business problem and Databricks' technical solution. You are a product manager for the field, owning the technical and product direction of the engagement from initial discovery through production launch and adoption. You will build C-suite trust, perform deep discovery to map the customer's political and technical landscape, and scope the value. You will define the Minimum Viable Product for a pilot, write the PRD that guides the engineering team, and manage the project to a successful landing. You will also lead technical discovery, shape solution architecture with FDEs, and ensure that each proposed solution can move from prototype to production. This role requires a rare combination of executive presence, deep product thinking, technical depth, and a hands-on delivery mindset. The impact you will have C-Suite Scoping & Value Definition: Partner with Sales to perform deep discovery, map the customer's organization, quantify the business value of $10M+ problems, and define the pilot, including its MVP, success criteria, and timeline. End-to-End Product Ownership: Author the PRD, prioritize the engineering backlog, manage scope, and act as the primary hands-on QA tester. Translate business requirements into clear data, integration, security, and operational requirements that engineers can build against. Technical Solution Leadership & Delivery: Drive the FDE build team through an agile delivery process, manage stakeholders from the C-suite to individual engineers, and unblock technical or organizational issues. Lead technical discovery and design reviews. Understand the customer's data flows, integrations, platform constraints, and operational environment; pressure-test architecture choices; and identify technical risks early. Solution Launch & Landing: Own the "Day 0" launch, manage the war room, and drive the solution from launch to full adoption by capturing user feedback, iterating, and proving the defined business value. Own production readiness across data quality, testing, security, performance, and operations. Work with the team to diagnose issues and drive them to resolution. Strategic Handoff & Growth: Scope the ongoing maintenance plan, create customer documentation/training, and leverage your trusted advisor status to identify the next high-value FDE engagement. Codify reusable solution patterns and bring field insights back to Product and Engineering. What we look for Executive Presence & Communication: You are a trusted advisor with strong executive presence and excellent communication skills. You are confident and humble, can build rapport quickly, and can help senior stakeholders make difficult decisions. Product Judgment & Delivery: You can define what to build and why, write strong product requirements, prioritize engineering work, manage scope, and lead complex agile software projects from an ambiguous problem to a measurable outcome. Technical Fluency & Architecture Judgment: You understand modern data and AI architectures, including cloud platforms, data pipelines, data models, distributed systems, APIs, security and governance, machine learning, and generative AI application patterns. You can lead architecture discussions, evaluate trade-offs, and pressure-test technical decisions. Hands-on Technical Ability: You are proficient in at least one language such as Python, Java, or SQL. You can explore data, work in notebooks, read and review code and pipelines, build or adapt prototypes, and contribute meaningfully to troubleshooting. Relevant Experience: Typically 7+ years of experience delivering complex, customer-facing data, analytics, AI, or software engagements, or equivalent experience as a founder or technical builder. You have helped deliver data, machine learning, or generative AI systems into production and understand the integration, operational, and adoption challenges that appear in real environments. Experience in a high-growth technology company, forward-deployed organization, or leading consultancy is valuable. You enjoy working onsite with customers (often 25-50%, sometimes higher) to drive delivery. About Databricks Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. raw.description:
Headquarters: Remote - India

About the Team

The FDE (Forward Deployed Engineering) team is a new, strategic initiative sponsored from the CEO and Founders down. Our mission is to win C-suite-sponsored, high-value AI opportunities by selling and delivering outcomes, not just a platform.

You will be part of the founding team, embedded with our most strategic customers from the very first sales call, all the way through to a production-ready solution. You will be the "product manager" for the customer's problem, responsible for the "why" and "what," while our FDEs (Engineers) will be your partners responsible for the "how."

Role Description

As a Deployment Strategist (DS), you are the critical bridge between a customer's multi-million-dollar business problem and Databricks' technical solution. You are a product manager for the field, owning the technical and product direction of the engagement from initial discovery through production launch and adoption.

You will build C-suite trust, perform deep discovery to map the customer's political and technical landscape, and scope the value. You will define the Minimum Viable Product for a pilot, write the PRD that guides the engineering team, and manage the project to a successful landing. You will also lead technical discovery, shape solution architecture with FDEs, and ensure that each proposed solution can move from prototype to production.

This role requires a rare combination of executive presence, deep product thinking, technical depth, and a hands-on delivery mindset.

The impact you will have

  • C-Suite Scoping & Value Definition: Partner with Sales to perform deep discovery, map the customer's organization, quantify the business value of $10M+ problems, and define the pilot, including its MVP, success criteria, and timeline.
  • End-to-End Product Ownership: Author the PRD, prioritize the engineering backlog, manage scope, and act as the primary hands-on QA tester. Translate business requirements into clear data, integration, security, and operational requirements that engineers can build against.
  • Technical Solution Leadership & Delivery: Drive the FDE build team through an agile delivery process, manage stakeholders from the C-suite to individual engineers, and unblock technical or organizational issues. Lead technical discovery and design reviews. Understand the customer's data flows, integrations, platform constraints, and operational environment; pressure-test architecture choices; and identify technical risks early.
  • Solution Launch & Landing: Own the "Day 0" launch, manage the war room, and drive the solution from launch to full adoption by capturing user feedback, iterating, and proving the defined business value. Own production readiness across data quality, testing, security, performance, and operations. Work with the team to diagnose issues and drive them to resolution.
  • Strategic Handoff & Growth: Scope the ongoing maintenance plan, create customer documentation/training, and leverage your trusted advisor status to identify the next high-value FDE engagement. Codify reusable solution patterns and bring field insights back to Product and Engineering.

What we look for

  • Executive Presence & Communication: You are a trusted advisor with strong executive presence and excellent communication skills. You are confident and humble, can build rapport quickly, and can help senior stakeholders make difficult decisions.
  • Product Judgment & Delivery: You can define what to build and why, write strong product requirements, prioritize engineering work, manage scope, and lead complex agile software projects from an ambiguous problem to a measurable outcome.
  • Technical Fluency & Architecture Judgment: You understand modern data and AI architectures, including cloud platforms, data pipelines, data models, distributed systems, APIs, security and governance, machine learning, and generative AI application patterns. You can lead architecture discussions, evaluate trade-offs, and pressure-test technical decisions.
  • Hands-on Technical Ability: You are proficient in at least one language such as Python, Java, or SQL. You can explore data, work in notebooks, read and review code and pipelines, build or adapt prototypes, and contribute meaningfully to troubleshooting.
  • Relevant Experience: Typically 7+ years of experience delivering complex, customer-facing data, analytics, AI, or software engagements, or equivalent experience as a founder or technical builder. You have helped deliver data, machine learning, or generative AI systems into production and understand the integration, operational, and adoption challenges that appear in real environments. Experience in a high-growth technology company, forward-deployed organization, or leading consultancy is valuable. You enjoy working onsite with customers (often 25-50%, sometimes higher) to drive delivery.

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog.
