title: Technical Customer Support
description: QuickMail is a cold email and LinkedIn outreach platform for markets you can't afford to burn. Our customers can't easily replace leads that land in spam, which is why deliverability matters more to us than anything else. We have been running since 2014, and we pioneered deliverability technology such as Inbox rotationâ¢ and deliverability AIâ¢. The Role We are hiring a technical customer support person with an owner's mentality. You will own support for QuickMail and Mailflow, our deliverability add-on. There is no first or second line. You are the first and last person our customers talk to. Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are. The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking. This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer. We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it. If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you. What Work Looks Like You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable. Every day Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it. Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution. Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform. Delighting customers Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast, and setting them up for success. Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked. Share customer feedback with the team, ask happy customers for reviews and case studies, and watch NPS for testimonial candidates. Making support smarter with AI Improve the AI support agent. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off. Write and maintain automated tests, built with AI, that try to break staging before customers do. Use the MCP connections we have in place (Helpscout, GitHub, Postmark, and others) to get an accurate picture of support and find the next thing worth improving. Keeping the product solid Gatekeep releases. New fixes and features land on staging every week. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected. Report bugs as GitHub issues with everything the developer needs: steps to reproduce, screenshots or a Loom, and any GraphQL or console errors. Captain red alerts. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice. Running the week Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated. Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps. Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude. Who You Are You build rapport fast. You are warm, positive, and relatable in writing and on calls. You are a good communicator. Externally, you can show warmth, empathy and care. Internally, you are able to communicate clearly and concisely about important things. You can operate with minimal instructions. You understand a short brief without every detail spelled out. You can prioritize well (especially when you have a lot on your plate), and get things done without hand-holding. You are comfortable on video. You are natural on live calls with Zoom and Meet, and on recorded video through tools like Loom. Your teammates can always count on you. You say what you'll do and you do what you said. You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity. You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results. You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack. Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive. Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are. A Plus If You Have Experience with customer facing work, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role. Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup. We can teach this, but a head start helps. Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client. Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report. An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment. How We Work Together You'll work directly with the founder and with our lead developer. Working with the founder can be intense. Here is what that looks like in practice: Replies are short and can come across as harsh. If something written lands badly or isn't clear, ask. Direction can change. The founder may say one thing, then something different a few days later as they learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt. Information should be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if asked. The founder can stay frustrated about a problem until it's solved. That's something they are aware of and working on. You'll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on. The team often thinks fast and interrupts each other when discussing ideas. If that would bother you, this role probably isn't for you. This role suits someone with high emotional intelligence, who doesn't take things personally, asks when something is unclear, and keeps many things moving at once. Your schedule can be flexible. If you have a martial arts class every Thursday at 3 pm, go and make up the time later. In return, on the rare occasion the team needs your help on a weekend, we ask you to be flexible too. Benefits Contract type: full-time or part-time Compensation: $2,500 to $4,000 USD per month, depending on experience and location. US-based hires will work as independent contractors (1099). Start date: negotiable Please mention the word **TRUMP** and tag RNzQuMjM1LjcwLjIyNw== when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RNzQuMjM1LjcwLjIyNw==). This is a beta feature to avoid spam applicants. Companies can search these words to find applicants that read this and see they're human.

title: Software Engineer - Data Platform
description: Headquarters: Remote - United States About Vercel: Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience. Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide. About the Role We're looking for a Staff level Engineer to lead the design and development of a next-generation Data Platform at Vercel. This is a unique opportunity to architect a foundational system that will power data across our products and business, supporting everything from real-time analytics to AI/ML initiatives. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Data Engineering, you'll define the technical vision for our data ecosystem, work across the organization to align engineering strategy with product goals, and build scalable, reliable systems using modern technologies like Kafka, ClickHouse, Tinybird, and Snowflake. You'll lead from the front, writing production-grade code, setting high standards for design and data governance, and mentoring a team of engineers as the organization grows. If you're excited by the challenge of building scalable data systems that drive product innovation, we'd love to hear from you. What You Will Do Design and implement a next-generation data platform that supports diverse requirements, including batch and real-time integrations, advanced analytics, and multiple data types, leveraging Kafka, Kafka-based tooling, and additional streaming technologies to power real-time data movement and processing. Work with engineering, product, and senior leadership teams across Vercel to architect solutions that address business needs, aligning technical strategies with product goals and ensuring seamless data availability and usability. Define and maintain guidelines for data ingestion, creation, enrichment, and storage, while overseeing data modeling, ETL processes, and data warehousing (ClickHouse, Tinybird, Snowflake) to achieve low-latency analytics and scalable storage. Develop end-to-end solutions across the tech stack, setting the example for engineering excellence, and provide mentorship and direction that fosters continuous improvement and innovation in the team. Partner with Security, Compliance, and Legal teams to ensure adherence to data protection standards, and champion high availability and fault tolerance through comprehensive monitoring, alerting, and incident response practices. Drive architectural decisions and roadmap planning that ensure efficiency, scalability, and high performance, and evaluate build-vs-buy trade-offs, integrating vendor solutions where appropriate. Collaborate with data scientists and machine learning teams to evolve infrastructure that supports advanced analytics and AI initiatives, serving as a key contributor to strategy, tooling, and platform enhancements for ML-related workloads. Act as a key decision-maker for discovering, vetting, and selecting data architectures and technologies critical to Vercel's success, and establish multi-phase strategic roadmaps that align with overall business objectives and drive data platform maturity. About You 8+ years of experience in data engineering, data architecture, or related roles, with at least 5 years at the Principal Engineer level. Proven track record designing and operating large-scale data infrastructures at high scale in a complex, fast-paced environment, with experience across Kafka and its ecosystem (e.g., Kafka Streams, Confluent Platform), ClickHouse, Tinybird, Snowflake, and broader big data frameworks. Proficiency in cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and associated big data services. Strong background in data governance and security, and adept at ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and protecting sensitive information. Outstanding communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence technical and non-technical stakeholders across varying organizational levels. A leadership mindset, with demonstrated ability to mentor teams, drive consensus, and advocate for best practices across the organization. A Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field is preferred. Industry recognition or notable contributions in data engineering (e.g., published works, open-source contributions) is a plus. Compensation & Benefits: Competitive compensation package, including equity. Inclusive Healthcare Package. Learn and Grow - we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills. Flexible Time Off. We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed. The San Francisco, CA base pay range for this role is $232,000 - $348,000. Actual salary will be based on job-related skills, experience, and location. Compensation outside of San Francisco may be adjusted based on employee location. The total compensation package may include benefits, equity-based compensation, and eligibility for a company bonus or variable pay program depending on the role. Your recruiter can share more details during the hiring process. Disclosures: Privacy: Please review our Job Applicant Privacy Policy for more information on how we handle your data. Equal Opportunity: Vercel is committed to fostering and empowering an inclusive community within our organization. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Vercel encourages everyone to apply for our available positions, even if they don't necessarily check every box on the job description. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/vercel-software-engineer-data-platform

description: Fuel50 is a workforce transformation platform helping organisations understand workforce capability, build skills and enable internal mobility in an AI-driven world. Our products combine skills intelligence, talent marketplace experiences and responsible AI to help people and organisations take their next step.Â We are looking for a Product Design Lead to shape the next chapter of our product experience and design organisation.Â This is a senior player-coach role. You will lead and develop our product design team while staying close to the work, setting direction, shaping product strategy, prototyping ideas and helping teams ship high-quality experiences.Â You will work closely with Product and Engineering as a leadership trio, influencing decisions across the organisation and helping Fuel50 build products that are simple, trusted and valuable.Â If youâre a strategic design leader who still loves getting close to the work, developing people and shipping real product, weâd love to hear from you!Â What you'll do: Lead, manage and coach our product designers, supporting their growth and helping them reach their next level.Â Set and communicate a clear product design vision across Fuel50's skills intelligence, talent mobility and AI-powered experiences, and tell the story of where our products are going in a way that excites customers, colleagues and leadership.Â Own the design direction without waiting for it to be handed to you. Spot opportunities, form a point of view, and prototype ideas to make them tangible.Â Bring a strong point of view to senior conversations, challenge assumptions constructively and influence decisions across the business.Â Partner with Product and Engineering from discovery through to delivery, balancing customer value, design quality, technical reality and pace.Â Design human-centred AI experiences with appropriate trust, explainability, user control and clear handoffs, including agent and assistant experiences that work across multiple surfaces such as the Fuel50 platform, Microsoft Teams and Copilot.Â Grow our design engineering capability, and be comfortable building and shipping working prototypes or code yourself.Â Evolve our design system, accessibility standards (including WCAG compliance) and design-to-code practices so Fuel50 feels coherent and high quality across every product.Â Shape design team structure, capability, hiring, planning and ways of working as the organisation evolves.Â What you'll bring: Experience in product design in a SaaS or technology environment (we suggest 7 or more years), including at least 2 years leading, managing or coaching designers, and a track record of building healthy, high-performing teams.Â Strong product design craft across discovery, interaction design, visual design, prototyping, research and shipped digital products.Â Experience designing complex, connected systems and journeys for multiple personas, ideally in an enterprise or B2B product.Â The ability to think big and set a compelling vision, while staying pragmatic about what can be learned and shipped next.Â The ability to originate ideas and direction, and to communicate them clearly through stories, prototypes and design narrative.Â Confidence working with experienced senior stakeholders and influencing through clarity, judgement and strong communication.Â Experience working closely with Product and Engineering as a genuine cross-functional trio.Â Technical fluency and a willingness to get into the code. You should be comfortable building working prototypes using HTML, CSS, JavaScript or similar tools, and have contributed code that has shipped to production, for example front-end changes or design system components submitted through pull requests.Â Hands-on experience using AI coding and design tools, such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, to prototype faster and ship real work. We want someone who uses these tools well and can show how they have changed the way their team works.Â Working knowledge of accessibility and WCAG. You have designed to WCAG standards, tested for it, and built accessibility into your team's design system and review process.Â An interest in design systems and data-informed decision-making.Â You do not need to tick every box. We care about the quality of your thinking, the way you work with people and your ability to turn ambitious ideas into better product experiences.Â All Fuellies are a core part of our culture and making Fuel50 an amazing place to work. Some additional benefits are:Â Â A day off on your birthday and your Fuel50 anniversaryÂ A âReFuel Dayâ once a quarter to relax and refuelÂ Remote work and flexible work times - we're supportive of school commitments, traveling in off-peak hours, and attending to lifeâs eventsÂ A progressive parental leave policyÂ Comprehensive fully subsidised health insurance with Southern CrossÂ What's it like to be a Fuellie? title: Software Engineer - Query Execution
description: Headquarters: Portugal - Remote Be Part of Building the Future Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. Based on open source technologies, including Apache Iceberg and Apache Arrow, Dremio provides an open lakehouse architecture enabling the fastest time to insight and platform flexibility at a fraction of the cost. Learn more at www.dremio.com. About the role Dremio’s Query Execution team builds the runtime responsible for executing analytical queries at scale. The team sits between query planning and table scans, building the systems that turn query plans into efficient, reliable execution. As a Software Engineer, you’ll work with experienced engineers to build, test, and support well-scoped improvements to the execution engine. You’ll learn how Dremio’s query runtime works while contributing to areas such as query operators, expression evaluation, memory management, scheduling, and performance. What you’ll be doing Build and support execution-engine components: Implement, test, debug, and maintain well-defined changes to query operators, expression evaluation, execution scheduling, and resource management. Develop reliable software: Write clear, maintainable Java code; add unit and integration tests; and follow established engineering practices for code review, testing, and documentation. Investigate issues: Help diagnose query correctness, reliability, and performance issues using query profiles, logs, telemetry, benchmarks, and production data. Learn runtime and performance fundamentals: Build familiarity with vectorized processing, concurrency, memory usage, parallelism, data exchange, and disk spilling. Collaborate with the team: Work closely with senior engineers and partner teams to understand requirements, break work into manageable tasks, and deliver incremental improvements. Use AI-assisted development tools: Apply AI tools to code comprehension, debugging, test generation, and documentation, while validating results through testing, review, and sound engineering judgment. Grow your engineering skills: Participate actively in design discussions and code reviews, seek feedback, and steadily take on broader technical responsibility. What we’re looking for Software engineering foundation: Up to two years of professional software development experience, or equivalent experience through internships, coursework, or substantial personal projects. Programming skills: Proficiency in Java or another object-oriented programming language; willingness to learn and work in a large Java codebase. Computer science fundamentals: Understanding of data structures, algorithms, and basic concurrency concepts. Problem-solving ability: Able to work through well-defined technical problems, ask good questions, and apply feedback to reach a solution. Quality mindset: Commitment to writing tested, maintainable code and learning established development, testing, and review practices. Communication and collaboration: Able to communicate progress, surface blockers early, and work effectively with teammates. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Bonus points if you have Exposure to database internals, query processing, distributed systems, or large-scale data processing. Familiarity with performance-oriented software concepts such as profiling, memory management, concurrency, or vectorized processing. Experience with C++, Apache Arrow, Parquet, Apache Iceberg, Spark, Hadoop, or cloud object stores. Contributions to open-source projects. What we value At Dremio, we hold ourselves to high standards when it comes to People, Thinking, and Action. Our Gnarlies (that's what we call our employees) communicate with clarity, drive accountability, and are respectful towards each other. We confront brutal facts and focus on results while operating with a sense of urgency and building a "flywheel". People who like to jump in and drive momentum will thrive in our #GnarlyLife. Dremio is an equal opportunity employer supporting workforce diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other unlawful factor. Dremio is committed to providing any necessary accommodations for individuals with disabilities within our application and interview process. To request accommodation due to a disability, please inform your recruiter. Dremio has policies in place to protect the personal information that employees and applicants disclose to us. Please click here to review the privacy notice. Important Security Notice for Candidates At Dremio, we uphold trust and transparency as paramount values in all our interactions with customers, partners, employees, and the general public. We have been targeted by individuals creating fake domains similar to ours to scam prospects and candidates. Please note that all official communications from us will be from an @dremio.com domain. If you suspect you've been targeted by a scam, it's imperative to report the incident to your local law enforcement agencies. For more information about this type of scam, please refer to Dremio's official statement here . Help design and maintain our infrastructure-as-code foundation, evolving the patterns and shared components other teams build on. Design and maintain the networking layer that connects Webflow's services, ensuring reliability, security, and scalability across our cloud environments. Help make observability data the foundation of how we operate, improving the dashboards, alerts, and SLOs for the infrastructure you own so that issues are caught before customers notice, and on-call pages are actionable instead of noisy. Build and maintain AI-powered automation that improves how we manage cloud infrastructure, from policy-as-code and drift detection to LLM-assisted runbook generation. Help define the culture of this growing team as it expands its international presence. Have 5+ years of experience owning and operating cloud infrastructure in a customer-facing environment that allows for little to no downtime. Have deep hands-on experience with AWS and a strong opinion on what good cloud operations look like. Have experience managing Kubernetes clusters at scale, including upgrades, node group management, autoscaling, and cluster add-on lifecycle. Have experience with infrastructure-as-code tools like Pulumi or Terraform, and a strong preference for changes made through code, not consoles. Have experience navigating multi-region or multi-cloud environments on AWS or GCP. Stay curious and open to growth, demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact. Have experience with OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Prometheus or Grafana Experience building AI-assisted infrastructure tooling, including cost optimization loops, anomaly detection, or policy-as-code with LLM assistance. Every permanent Webflower receives equity (RSUs) in our growing, privately held company. Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums. Support for every stage of family life . 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions. Time off that’s actually off. Localized support for work and wellness expenses — from Wi-Fi to workouts. Bonus for building together. title: Abuse Research Engineer
description: Headquarters: Remote from the US Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities. What you’ll do As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Headquarters: Remote from the US

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence.  Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains.  Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.

About Magic Eden and Dicey
Magic Eden reached unicorn status in just 9 months after launch, one of the fastest in history. We built a category-defining NFT marketplace from scratch and proved we know how to move fast. Now we're doing it again. Dicey is our crypto casino and sportsbook platform, targeting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets.

We're a small, fully remote team. We ship fast, we're hands-on with our data, and we're rebuilding how a growth team operates around AI from the ground up.

The role
Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.

This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. It's explicitly AI-native. You'll build workflows, agents, and pipelines to run lifecycle campaigns that would have taken a whole team two years ago. Half the job is identifying the right problem. The other half is running the experiments to find the answer.

What you'll do

  • Own retention and monetization as a growth loop. Set the targets, find the leverage, and drive the numbers for everything that happens after a player signs up

  • Own the player segmentation framework. Today it's value and risk. You decide how it evolves, what signals feed it, and how the rest of the company uses it

  • Build the AI-native growth stack. Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work

  • Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Size them, spec them, ship them, measure them

  • Spend real time in our data warehouse and on-chain data finding patterns and turn them into campaigns before anyone else does

  • Expand the signals we have on players: on-chain activity, status-match programs, social account linking, and whatever else you can think of

  • Run the campaigns. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting

  • Partner with engineering and design to ship the product surfaces that make all of this repeatable

What we're looking for

  • Strong intuition for player psychology and incentive design. Experience in gambling, gaming, fintech, or consumer marketplaces helps. Genuine curiosity about why people behave the way they do is required

  • Deeply analytical. You can go from a vague question to a clean cohort cut yourself, without waiting on a data scientist

  • AI-native by default. You already use AI to write queries, build analyses, and automate your own work and you want to push that much further

  • High output with good judgment. You generate a lot of ideas and know which ones are worth testing first

  • Bias to do it yourself. You're comfortable sending the email, running the query, and writing the spec, not just briefing others

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. There's no playbook here, you'll be building it

Backgrounds that tend to fit

  • Growth PM at a data-heavy consumer company

  • MBB consultant who wants to move into product and own outcomes, not just advise on them

  • Product Minded Data scientist or analyst who wants to ship, not just report

Why this is interesting

  • Competitive, top-of-market compensation

  • You're defining what a growth PM looks like in an AI-native company, there's no inherited playbook

  • Personalised retention is where the industry is going and we're building it early

  • Real ownership: a segmentation framework, a product surface, and a P&L lever, with a direct line to the founding team

title: Frontend Engineer
description: About ActAI There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting. Our application focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations Our objective is to organise anyone's life. Â Role As a Web Frontend Engineer, you will build the core web experiences, including Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets. You will own complex, highly interactive product surfaces from architecture through implementation, working closely with product, design, backend and AI engineers to make AI a native part of how users communicate, write, organise and work. Â What You'll Own Build major web experiences across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs, and Sheets. Develop complex interactions including real-time messaging, collaborative editing, rich-text editing, scheduling, tables, and spreadsheets. Build reusable frontend architecture and components that work consistently across ActAI applications. Integrate streaming AI responses, proactive actions, and model-driven experiences directly into product workflows. Own frontend performance, responsiveness, reliability and accessibility across browsers and devices. Work closely with product and design to take ideas from prototype to production quickly. Â What We're Looking For Strong experience building complex, production web applications using React, TypeScript and modern frontend technologies. Deep understanding of frontend architecture, state management, browser APIs, and performance. Experience building highly interactive products such as chat, collaboration, productivity, document editing, calendars, or workspaces. Experience with real-time systems, WebSockets, streaming APIs, or collaborative interfaces. Strong product and UI judgment with attention to interaction details. Able to independently own features from technical design through production. Â Outcomes Users can communicate, write, organise and collaborate seamlessly across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets. Complex interactions such as group messaging, editing, scheduling and collaboration feel fast and reliable. AI capabilities are integrated naturally into product workflows rather than added as separate chatbot experiences. Frontend architecture remains fast, maintainable and reusable as ActAI expands into new applications and workflows. Â Tech Stack TypeScript React.js / Next.js HTML / CSS WebSockets / streaming APIs Node.js REST / GraphQL APIs Â How We Work The best products today in the world were built by small, world-class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively and move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high-quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment and execute independently. Our goal is to put in the hands of our users a truly magical product. Â Interview Process If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 3, but no more than 4 interviews. Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite. We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us and help bring practical AI benefits to billions of users globally. title: Marketing Student Assistant
description:
Marketing Student Assistant

Are you studying marketing, communications or business and looking for a student job where you can build hands-on marketing experience and see how it all comes together in practice?

Weâre looking for a structured and proactive Marketing Student Assistant to join our Brand & Marketing team at Copenhagen Optimization.

Youâll work alongside our Head of Marketing, Growth Marketing Manager and Content Strategist, helping us turn plans into action across digital, events, content and campaigns. Itâs a hands-on role with plenty of variety and room to take on more responsibility as you grow.

What you'll work on

  • Website & digital: Update and maintain website content, event and campaign pages, and help keep everything accurate and up to date.

  • Events: Support conferences and events around the world â from registrations and exhibitor portals to materials, print orders, attendee lists and deadlines.

  • Content & campaigns: Support campaign execution by preparing content assets, landing pages, lists and other campaign elements.

  • Marketing coordination: Keep calendars, project pages, assets and plans organized, coordinate smaller deliverables and follow-ups, and help make sure the practical details don't fall between the cracks.

  • Creative support: Help adapt or create simple marketing materials and visuals. Experience with Canva, Figma or similar tools is a plus.

Who we're looking for

You are studying marketing, communications, business or a related field, ideally with at least one or two years of your studies remaining.

You like creating structure, following things through and seeing a task go from idea to done. Youâre dependable, attentive to detail and comfortable taking initiative. We donât expect you to know everything from day one â what matters is that youâre curious, eager to learn and interested in how marketing works in practice.

You:

  • Communicate confidently in English, both written and spoken.

  • Work in a structured way and keep track of tasks and deadlines.

  • Take initiative and care about the quality of what you deliver.

  • Are comfortable working with digital tools. We use HubSpot, Notion, Dropbox and LinkedIn, but you don't need to know them all already.

  • Are interested in marketing and keen to learn across different disciplines.

Who is Copenhagen Optimization?

Copenhagen Optimization is the company behind Better Airport, our software platform built for intelligent airport operations.

We work with airports around the world to connect planning, resource management, staffing and day-of operations, enabling them to make better operational decisions every day.

Founded in Copenhagen in 2014, we have offices in Copenhagen and Boston and customers across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and beyond.

What we offer

Approximately 15â20 hours per week, with flexibility around your studies, exams and personal life. Youâll join a small marketing team, work closely with experienced colleagues across the business and gain hands-on experience in international B2B marketing.

Weâre looking for someone who wants to stay with us for the longer term, become part of the team and gradually take on more responsibility.

Interested?

Send us your application and CV and tell us a little about yourself, why this role interests you and what you think you'd bring to the team.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and may fill the position once we've found the right person.

title: Senior Specialist Global QMS
description:
More than one million people in the United States today are fighting blood cancer. While a traditional allogeneic stem cell transplant has been the best hope for many, the transplant itself can prove fatal or lead to serious conditions, such as graft vs. host disease. Orca Bio is a commercial-stage biotechnology company redefining the transplant process by developing next-generation cell therapies with the goal of providing significantly better survival rates with dramatically fewer risks. With our purified, high-precision cell therapies we hope to not only replace patients' blood and immune systems with healthy ones, but also restore their lives. The Senior Specialist, Global QMS will help implement Orca Bioâs global quality management system across all sites. This role will support and lead the internal audit program, supplier management program, and inspection readiness. This role will support the growth and expansion of the global quality program to support manufacturing of our cell therapy products. You will help establish, implement and maintain the audit program across Orca Bio sites to ensure compliance with GxP and regulatory expectations. Your role will support Orca Bios commercial readiness and ongoing clinical programs by managing and facilitating audits, resolving supplier-related quality issues and interacting with quality management teams at the site levels to ensure consistent application of quality systems across the organization. 
 Responsibilities: Plan, schedule and execute internal audits across all sites and functions in accordance with the internal audit program. Develop audit agenda, conduct interviews, review processes and generate audit reports. Support the global Quality Management Review (QMR) process, ensuring timely data collection, analysis, and reporting to senior leadership. Support the supplier qualification and management program, including risk assessments, supplier audits, and ongoing monitoring to ensure compliance with GxP requirements. Drive global inspection management activities, ensuring cross-functional and site readiness for FDA, EMA, and other health authority inspections. Provide oversight and guidance to site QMR administrators ensuring consistent quality system implementation across all Orca Bio sites. Establish and monitor global QMS key performance indicators (KPIs), oversee trending of quality metrics, and ensure data-driven insights are used to improve quality systems and performance. Partner with IT and business process owners to identify and implement QMS system enhancements, including defining requirements, driving prioritization and ensuring changes are validated and compliant. Review, approve, and provide quality oversight for validation documentation (e.g., equipment qualification, computer system validation, process validation) for global enterprise systems (e.g. MasterControl, ERP systems, Trackwise, etc.) ensuring alignment with regulatory and internal requirements. Collaborate with cross-functional and site leadership teams to drive continuous improvement initiatives, ensuring the QMS evolves in line with business needs and regulatory expectations. Experience: Bachelorâs degree in a scientific or engineering discipline required; advanced degree preferred. Minimum 5+ years of relevant Quality Assurance or Quality Systems experience in a GxP-regulated environment, with at least 2-3 years in a leadership role. Strong knowledge of global quality regulations and standards (FDA, EMA, ICH, ISO 9001, 21 CFR Parts 210/211/820, EU GMP). Proven experience leading Quality Management Review, internal audit programs, supplier management processes, and validation oversight. Demonstrated success in establishing and trending quality performance metrics and KPIs. Experience supporting and/or administering electronic QMS systems and partnering with IT for system enhancements. Experience working in a multi-site or global quality organization strongly preferred. Excellent organizational, analytical, and communication skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across functional and site boundaries. 
 $90,000 - $120,000 a year 
 The anticipated annual salary range for this job is based on prior experience in the role/industry, education, location, internal equity, and other job-related factors as permitted by law. For remote-based positions, this range may vary based on your local market. Full-time employment positions will also be eligible to receive pre-IPO equity and annual bonus, in addition to competitive medical, dental, and vision benefits, PTO, 401(k) plan, life and accidental death and disability coverage, and parental leave benefits. Other perks include subsidized daily lunches and snacks at our on-site locations. Who we are We are driven by a passion for science and compassion for patients. We act with urgency to ensure our treatments are one day accessible to all who need them. We live by our core values of passion, courage, and integrity. Excellence in our work means the chance to unlock a better quality of life for our patients, and with that comes tremendous responsibility. We innovate on a path that hasnât been paved. We embrace an entrepreneurial spirit and take calculated risks to achieve our mission. We arenât afraid to ask âwhy notâ and challenge the status quo. We maintain a start-up culture of camaraderie and leadership by example, regardless of title. Weâre proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and recognize that celebrating our differences creates stronger, lasting solutions that better serve our team, our patients and their healthcare providers. Notice to staffing firms Orca Bio does not accept resumes from staffing agencies with which we do not have a written agreement and specific engagement for a particular opening. Our employment activities, inquiries and offers are managed through our HR/Talent team, and all candidates are presented through this channel only. We do not accept unsolicited resumes, and we rarely outsource recruitment. For over twenty years, Chaos has developed innovative technologies serving multiple industries, including architecture and design, media and entertainment, and product e-commerce. Chaosâ solutions help architects, designers, VFX artists/animators, and other creative professionals share ideas, optimize workflows, and create immersive experiences. Headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, Chaos is a global company with offices in 11 cities worldwide. In 2022, Chaos and Enscape merged, bringing together two industry-leading companies into one. Since then, Chaos has continued to grow with the additions of Cylindo, AXYZ Design, and Evolve Lab, further expanding our expertise and solutions across architecture, design, e-commerce, and AI. For more information, please visit chaos.com . Role Overview The Team Lead, Education Sales leads the Education sales team and owns the end-to-end go-to-market strategy for the Education segment, covering both University and Student markets. The role is responsible for driving new institution and student customer acquisition, growing ARR within the existing base, and reducing churn across both segments. The University segment operates through direct, relationship-led sales to institutions, while the Student segment runs as a low-touch, digital-first purchase journey, requiring close partnership with the Ecommerce team to optimise the online funnel, conversion rates, and pricing experience. Reporting to the Sr. Director GTM Strategy & Transformation, this role requires a commercially driven sales leader with a hands-on approach, a track record of owning segment revenue end-to-end, and the ability to coach and develop a team while remaining personally active in deals. The role operates with a high degree of autonomy and suits someone who wants to build and scale a team rather than maintain one. Main Responsibilities Lead and develop the Education sales team, setting clear individual performance expectations, coaching from the front, and stepping into deals directly where needed to support pipeline and attainment targets. Drive expansion and retention within the existing student and institution customer base, identifying and executing initiatives that grow ARR and reduce churn. Own ARR and pipeline growth within the University segment through relationship-led, direct sales to institutions, tracking key performance metrics and diagnosing and correcting underperformance. Own ARR and seat growth within the Student segment, which runs as a low-touch, digital-first purchase journey rather than a traditional sales motion; partner with the Ecommerce team to continuously optimize the online funnel, conversion rates, and pricing experience. Own accurate pipeline forecasting and attainment reporting for the Education business, providing reliable visibility into performance for sales reviews and senior leadership. Partner with RevOps, Marketing, Product, and Ecommerce to ensure Education-specific campaigns, content, and product feedback are prioritised and executed effectively. Required Experience At least 5 years of sales experience within a SaaS or technology environment, including demonstrated experience leading a sales team with direct accountability for team performance and revenue outcomes. Proven track record of owning a direct sales territory or segment end-to-end, from pipeline generation through closed, retained revenue. Experience managing and influencing a low-touch, digital or ecommerce-led purchase journey (funnel, conversion, pricing) is a strong advantage. Previous experience in Architecture, Education, EdTech, or a related vertical is an advantage, but not required. Required Skills Takes full ownership of commercial outcomes: builds pipeline, closes deals, and drives team performance without waiting to be directed. Leads by example in the field: comfortable coaching team members through live deals and personally engaging in high-priority opportunities where it makes a difference. Translates ARR and revenue data into clear, defensible strategy, is able to identify where performance is off track, diagnose the root cause, and act on it. Communicates with credibility at senior level: presents team results, forecasts, and strategic needs clearly to VP-level and cross-functional stakeholders. Able to build effective working relationships and collaborate cross-functionally across Ecommerce, RevOps, and Marketing: driving digital funnel and conversion improvements for the Student segment without direct authority. Operates effectively with high autonomy in a fast-moving environment: sets own priorities, creates momentum without close direction, and holds a consistently high personal bar for execution and results. Familiarity with MEDDICC or a similar sales qualification framework is an advantage. We welcome people who value teamwork, stick to their commitments and are curious to explore new ways for achieving mastery. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done. Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma. Weâre building an AI scientist for our customers. We canât do that if we havenât built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today. ROLE OVERVIEW The Solutions Delivery Manager is responsible for ensuring Benchling solution development, coverage, efficacy, quality, and enablement across the Customer Experience team. Operating at the intersection of our product suite and our customers, this dynamic role focuses on translating our product capabilities into effective solutions to match our customers' scientific use cases, and enabling the broader CX organization to operationalize around Benchling's best practices. Solutions Delivery Manager works cross-functionally with Benchling's build organization, as well as across the CX departments, to develop robust solutions that can deliver value to our customers, while improving internal knowledge and productivity. Chemistry is one of Benchling's newest and most exciting product areas â unlocking an entirely new group of companies, scientists, and science to be done on Benchling. This role will help navigate a budding product area through to market adoption, partnering closely with internal product, enablement, and delivery teams, while working directly with customers to build trust and help shape our vision in this space. Successful Solutions Delivery Managers will harness the knowledge and experience Benchling has gained across thousands of customer engagements, and leverage previous and learned experience to serve as an expert across scientific domains and modalities served by Benchling. They will develop, and continuously improve our solutions as both the science and Benchling product capabilities evolve. A successful candidate will be comfortable working across teams and systems, often with no existing guidance or playbook, to deliver impactful solutions and value aligned with our department and team goals. We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

Weâre building an AI scientist for our customers. We canât do that if we havenât built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Solutions Delivery Manager is responsible for ensuring Benchling solution development, coverage, efficacy, quality, and enablement across the Customer Experience team. Operating at the intersection of our product suite and our customers, this dynamic role focuses on translating our product capabilities into effective solutions to match our customers' scientific use cases, and enabling the broader CX organization to operationalize around Benchling's best practices. Solutions Delivery Manager works cross-functionally with Benchling's build organization, as well as across the CX departments, to develop robust solutions that can deliver value to our customers, while improving internal knowledge and productivity.

Chemistry is one of Benchling's newest and most exciting product areas â unlocking an entirely new group of companies, scientists, and science to be done on Benchling. This role will help navigate a budding product area through to market adoption, partnering closely with internal product, enablement, and delivery teams, while working directly with customers to build trust and help shape our vision in this space.

Successful Solutions Delivery Managers will harness the knowledge and experience Benchling has gained across thousands of customer engagements, and leverage previous and learned experience to serve as an expert across scientific domains and modalities served by Benchling. They will develop, and continuously improve our solutions as both the science and Benchling product capabilities evolve. A successful candidate will be comfortable working across teams and systems, often with no existing guidance or playbook, to deliver impactful solutions and value aligned with our department and team goals.

Â 

RESPONSIBILITIES

Including, but not limited to:

  • Navigate a budding product area through to market adoption â partnering with internal product, enablement, and delivery teams, while working directly with customers to build trust and shape our vision in this space

  • Serve as a key advisor on customer accounts as an expert in the scientific and product space

  • Deliver services and oversee services engagements to ensure high quality solution and delivery

  • Build a roadmap of solution assets to deliver impactful solutions to the broader CX organization

  • Build and maintain solution assets, such as best practices documents

  • Train and educate the broader CX organization through various means (e.g. create documentation, drive enablement initiatives, refresh solutions, advise on customer engagements, etc.)

  • Collaborate across CX departments to reflect customer learnings into solution assets

  • Operationalize Benchlingâs new product introduction motions to deliver new product insights

  • Work cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, and Strategy teams to align on product value and customer messaging

  • Learn existing and new verticals that Benchling services

Â 

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Scientific and Benchling Knowledge

    • Fluency in medicinal chemistry or PD chemistry, ideally both

    • Fluency in a chemistry-focused lab informatics tool

    • Knowledge of Benchlingâs Platform and solutions, and technical proficiency with Benchling products is preferred

  • Customer Readiness

    • Experienced customer experience professional with a strong track record in overseeing the success of customer engagements

    • Superior customer service skills â the ability to be empathetic, accurate, resourceful, and conscientious with a sense of urgency

  • Problem Solving and Collaborative Success

    • Excellent oral and written communication skills to work effectively with others both inside and outside departmental boundaries, at remote locations and/or outside the company

    • Demonstrate ability to analyze and resolve complex problems and rapidly assimilate new knowledge and information

    • Flexible and able to adjust on the fly to new demands; a high sense of urgency, tendency towards action, and comfortable working through ambiguity to independently make progress on individual and team goals

  • Experience and Educational Requirements

    • 6+ years of lab experience in medicinal chemistry, PD chemistry, or a closely related field

    • 2+ years experience in customer service or customer-facing roles

    • Bachelor's degree in chemistry, or life sciences related field is required (biology, microbiology, genetics, biotechnology, neurology, etc.)

Another may go from developing training products for humanitarian workers (https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/solutions/defense/other-projects...) on to assistive technologies that make work easier for farmers around the world (https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/solutions/agriculture/other-agri...).

C++ and Python software engineers - https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/careers/software-engineer-2.html

ML/AI Engineering - https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/careers/software-engineer-machin...

That kind of unsubstantive comment is not cool on HN anywhere, but particularly not in the Who Is Hiring threads, where there's no opportunity to establish whether or not the accusation is true.

That account posted two nearly identical comments about completely different companies, and has zero other posting history here. Those are not good signs. If HN is going to have a job board, it's not fair to let just anyone come along, smear people's posts, and significantly affect their company's reputation, without any due process.

If that seems unduly restrictive to you, I understand. But we've seen many cases of people taking advantage of the public forum to smear others in dodgy or unfair ways. As I explained at that link above, bad corporate behavior is a thing, and bad internet commenter behavior is also a thing. An HN job thread is no place to adjudicate which is which, so we need to err on the side of not going there.

These kind of comments are (were?) the best part of this board. Where the OP also can chime in and respond... Even such responses are helpful to have an idea about the company. It's a huge time-saver.

This comment breaks the rules at the top. Please don't post these here.

More explanation at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=22667632.

Presidential Innovation Fellows | Washington, DC | ONSITE | Full-time

The Presidential Innovation Fellows (PIF) program is looking for high-performing data scientists, designers, engineers, executives, innovators, product managers, and technology strategists that care deeply about solving our nation’s most difficult challenges and want to deliver better products, services, and experiences to the American public.

The program is a highly selective, non-partisan, innovation fellowship that pairs talented mid-to-senior-level entrepreneurs and technologists with top government leaders to take on complex projects that have the potential for significant impact. It was launched in 2012 by former U.S. Chief Technology Officer Todd Park, and since then, more than 150 Fellows have worked within over 35 agencies. Over half of the Fellows have decided to stay in government after the program, and have gone on to lead new digital teams and serve as chief technology officers, chief information officers, chief data officers, and chief marketing officers at various agencies.

Fellows are building products and services at scale to serve all Americans. Select potential projects for the Fall 2020 cohort include:

• Assisting the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid modernize their technology stack so they can better share data with stakeholders across the healthcare ecosystem.

• Helping NASA speed up the discovery, analysis and development of aerospace systems using artificial intelligence to ultimately help combat climate change by reducing fuel burn for the aerospace industry.

• Working with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to better support veterans transitioning from military to civilian life, adopt medical innovations to improve mental health services and health outcomes, and reduce the processing time for benefits claims.

• Collaborating with multiple federal agencies to drive the adoption of AI technologies across government.

• Ensuring that the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a U.S. foreign aid agency, and their partner countries have the data, technology, and innovations skills needed to maximize the impact of U.S. investments.

• Guiding the Department of Transportation as they adapt to the challenges and opportunities that autonomous vehicles and aerial systems offer.

• Helping the U.S. Marine Corps conduct a digital and data transformation to keep Marines safe.

Apply today: https://apply.pif.gov

Learn more about us: https://presidentialinnovationfellows.gov

children.author: DoreenMichele
children.text:
It looks to me like no actual rule was broken per se, but GP is aware he was breaking more like a thing of etiquette. It's kind of an "apologies in advance, as I know this is sort of rude, but I'm going to say it anyway because I'm saying something nice" that wasn't phrased optimally.

HN generally discourages lightweight chit chat to protect the signal to noise ratio. They more strongly discourage it in these Hiring posts and it seems to me that's the correct way to handle it because this is intended as a free advertising space, not a discussion space.

In part for purposes of making advertisers comfortable posting here so they will post at all, HN more strictly forbids attacks against the advertisers because that would drive away a lot of advertisers and harm the utility of these posts. But, also, these posts have a lot of little ads and it's already a huge pile of info to sort through if you are job hunting, even without chit chat and ugly, long tangents thrown in.

HN likely doesn't have the manpower to lock these threads and institute a pre approval process as the mechanism that protects these posts as 99% (free) ads. So they rely on certain social expectations to make this work.

Since the membership very much values these posts, the membership generally does a good job of respecting certain expectations.

There are spaces on the internet where the meme is "This is why we can't have nice things" and it typically gets stated as a way to say "It's not the fault of incompetent moderation. No, the members are just assholes who won't behave." (Often stated by the mods, who are incompetent and prone to putting out the fire with gasoline.)

HN has both competent moderation and members who more or less try hard to behave. This is why we can have nice things around here, like the Who is Hiring threads, which are a free service benefiting both businesses in need of staff and people in need of employment.
out of curiosity, what HN law are you potentially breaking? I'm guessing there's a law that prohibits posts that simply say another comment is good?

rjyoungling
children.text: No, I totally get it! I didn't mean to accidentally imply that you were being unreasonable. I was merely being facetious about HN culture my friend!

If you mean the rule at the top, it's not up there to prevent comments like this, but rather the complaints that people sometimes post about their previous opinions/experiences with a company in reply to a job posting. We don't allow those because we don't have any way of knowing which are justified and which aren't. Bad corporate behavior is a thing,  disgruntled commenters are a thing (the kind who are good at telling only one misleading side of the story), and the two can be hard to tell apart. Sometimes the community can sort things out through the informal adjudication process that arises in HN threads around controversial questions—but those are lengthy and Who Is Hiring threads are not the place for it.

I'd appreciate from the downvoters how I can improve.

I'm a CS grad with some work experience (1 year dev, 1 year coding bootcamp teacher). See me as a junior that ramps up quicker than the average junior (e.g. last month I owned a lot of boxes at hackthebox.eu for fun and was a top 5% after 2 weeks of non-stop playing [1]).

The reason I'm not applying but simply writing things here is because I'm tired of applying (it's hard to hear more than 100+ "no" while at university you were a top student). But I do want to know if you guys think I'm worth considering.

Which is why I'm brutally honest with the following:

Companies tend to reject me due to lack of experience, and (in my opinion) undervalue how quick I can pick things up and how willing I am to work amazingly hard, especially at the beginning of a job. When they hire me they tend to be surprised with how wrong they were about me.

My strength is that I'm a generalist, much more so than most people. My weakness is that people have the perception that I can't be a specialist. But anyone that gave me a chance in hiring me during my freelance time know that I am capable of performing one role as a specialist (full-stack developer with a business and security mindset).

During my good days I tend to have an Elon Musk mindset. He says that working 80 to 100 hours per week means you learn 2 to 2.5 times faster, I mostly agree -- I think it is sometimes more because the interconnectness of things pushes the multiple a bit higher. During my bad days I simply want to work 40 hours per week go home and relax. During these times I sort of don't want to work due to stress, but know that I have to work because it keeps my mind sharp.

raw.description:
Position: Road and Trail Program Coordinator

Location: Remote within Canada

Reports to: Manager, Marketing and Events (Domestic Programs)

Classification: Contractor

Duration: 12 months

Overview

Athletics Canada is the national sport organization for track and field, cross county, road, mountain, and trail running. Its purpose is to support high performance athletics excellence at the domestic and international level and to provide leadership in developmental athletics in partnership with its provincial/territorial branch partners. Athletics Canada is a not-for-profit, charitable organization operating under a Board of Directors elected by provincial/territorial members.

The Job

Athletics Canada is seeking an organized, collaborative and passionate Road & Trail Program Coordinator to support the continued growth and development of road running, trail running and mountain running across Canada.

The successful candidate will play an important role in delivering Athletics Canada's national Road & Trail programs and services, working closely with Athletics Canada staff, Provincial/Territorial Branches, event organizers, athletes, coaches, and volunteers. The position will have direct responsibility for several national programs while also supporting the delivery of several Canadian Championships and the Mountain & Trail National Team.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who understands the culture and landscape of road, trail and mountain running and is excited by the opportunity to help build stronger, more accessible and better-connected programs across Canada.

The position reports to the Marketing & Events Manager, while working closely with the Director, Domestic Programs & Safe Sport on program development, policy implementation, governance and the broader Athletics Canada Road & Trail strategy.

Responsibilities

1. Program Development & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop strong relationships with Athletics Canada Branches, event organizers, clubs, athletes, coaches, officials and other stakeholders within the Road & Trail community.
  • Provide leadership to the Athletics Canada Off-Track Committee and related working groups.
  • Monitor developments within Canadian and international Road & Trail running and identify opportunities for program improvement.
  • Assist with communications, resources and educational materials for event organizers and participants.
  • Collect and maintain program data and provide regular updates and reports to Athletics Canada staff.
  • Contribute to broader Athletics Canada initiatives that support participation, athlete development, competition and excellence in Road & Trail running.


2. Road, Trail & Mountain Canadian Championships

Support the Marketing & Events Manager in the planning and delivery of Athletics Canada Road, Trail and Mountain Running Canadian Championships, including:

  • Assist with championship documentation, host selection, contracting, and coordination with host organizations.
  • Assist with event planning, timelines, communications and operational requirements.
  • Support championship eligibility, registration, technical and event information.
  • Support championship marketing and promotional activities.
  • Assist with post-event reporting, evaluation and continuous improvement.
  • Develop strong working relationships with Race Directors, Local Organizing Committees, and other event partners.

3. Road Race Label Program

Lead the ongoing delivery and development of the Athletics Canada Road Race Label Program, including:

  • Manage applications, label requirements, agreements and communications with approved Road Race Label events.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for event organizers
  • Coordinate event requirements, including sanctioning, course certification, technical requirements and other Athletics Canada standards.
  • Support the development and implementation of event benefits, marketing opportunities and athlete-facing communications.
  • Monitor program participation and identify opportunities to strengthen the quality, profile and reach of the national road race calendar.
  • Work with Athletics Canada staff and Branches to ensure consistent application of national requirements.

4. Mountain & Trail National Team

Support the delivery and development of Athletics Canada's Mountain & Trail National Team program, including:

  • Support Athletics Canada's participation in international mountain and trail running championships and events.
  • Assist with athlete and coach communications and team administration.
  • Support team selection, registration, travel and logistical planning.
  • Assist with national team event preparation and on-site team operations.
  • Contribute to the continued development of a strong and sustainable national mountain and trail running program.

5. Course Measurement & Certification

Coordinate the Athletics Canada Road Course Measurement & Certification Program, including:

  • Manage applications and communication with event organizers seeking course certification.
  • Maintain an accurate national database of certified courses and renewal dates.
  • Support the transition to updated course certification requirements and processes.
  • Provide guidance to event organizers regarding course measurement and certification requirements.
  • Help develop and coordinate pathways and training for certified course measurers.

6. National Road & Trail Sanctioning

Support the implementation and ongoing administration of the Athletics Canada Road & Trail Sanctioning Framework, including:

  • Work with Athletics Canada Provincial/Territorial Branches and event organizers to support adoption and implementation of national minimum requirements.
  • Assist with the development of tools, resources and communications to support consistent application across Canada.
  • Monitor implementation and identify areas requiring clarification, education or additional support.
  • Work closely with the Director, Domestic Programs & Safe Sport on policy implementation and governance matters.
  • Help ensure that Athletics Canada's national Road & Trail programs are aligned with broader organizational policies and strategic objectives.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of technical knowledge, organizational ability and a genuine understanding of the Road & Trail running community.

  • Understanding of the Road & Trail landscape – Knowledge of competition rules, age categories, competition formats and the culture of the road, trail and mountain running community. Familiarity with event management and delivery is strongly preferred.
  • Strong organizational skills – Ability to manage multiple programs, deadlines, projects and communications streams simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail.
  • Program coordination experience – Experience coordinating programs, events or projects, ideally within sport, nonprofit, community development or a similar environment.
  • Strong communication skills – Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with athletes, coaches, volunteers, event organizers and organizational partners.
  • Bilingualism – Fluency in both English and French is considered an asset.
  • Athlete and participant focused – Comfortable communicating directly with athletes and participants in an empathetic, respectful and responsive manner and able to work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds and at different stages of their athletic journey.
  • Collaborative mindset – Ability to work effectively with the Athletics Canada Off-Track Committee, Provincial/Territorial Branches, Local Organizing Committees and colleagues across Canada.
  • Solution-oriented approach – Proactively identifies opportunities to improve programs, solve problems and strengthen the overall Road & Trail system.
  • Independent and self-motivated – Comfortable working remotely and managing responsibilities independently while maintaining strong communication with colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Passion for sport – Genuine interest in running and a commitment to supporting the growth and development of Road & Trail running in Canada.

Work Location

This is a fully remote position based in Canada.

The position requires occasional evening and weekend work, particularly around competitions, meetings and national team activities.

Regular domestic travel will be required for Canadian Championships, national team activities, meetings and other Athletics Canada events.

Occasional international travel may be required in support of the Mountain & Trail National Team or other international activities.

The position requires the ability to work independently in a remote environment while maintaining effective communication and collaboration with colleagues and stakeholders across Canada.

To Apply

The application deadline is Sunday, November 15th, 2026. We thank all candidates who apply. Athletics Canada is an equal opportunity employer.
